text.p: These are leading stories in this morning's Paris newspapers.
-- Blue-chip CAC 40 index sets record closing high despite parliamentary election uncertainty, franc hits highest levels on Tuesday since National Assembly was dissolved on April 21.
-- Former Socialist Minister Dominique Strauss Kahn says in an interview the shift to a European single currency should be subject to a political discussion, notably with Germany.

-- Alcatel Alsthom chairman Serge Tchuruk and Dassault Industries chairman Serge Dassault said yesterday a victory by rival Lagardere in bid battle for state-controlled Thomson-CSF would lead to a break-up of the defence firm.

-- Finance Minister Jean Arthuis says in an interview his reform of the Treasury is to be implemented immediately, and is designed to ensure a better control of the state over state-owned firms. He adds the shift to a 35-hour work week advocated by the socialists would trigger an 11 percent rise in the cost of labour.
-- Compagnie Financiere de Paribas increases stake in Compagnie Bancaire to over 50 percent.
-- RPR centre-right party spokesman Jean-Francois Cope says in an interview he trusts the modernisation of the state will eventually trigger cuts in mandatory contributions.
-- President Jacques Chirac to begin state visit to China tomorrow.
-- Replacement of Eramet mining group chairman Yves Chambaud with Thierry Chambolle halted since the Eramet shareholders' meeting has been postponed until further notice.
